function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content:
Electricity isn’t something that was “discovered” by a single person—it’s a natural phenomenon that has been known since ancient times (e.g., static electricity observed by Thales of Miletus). The modern scientific understanding of electricity emerged gradually through the work of many scientists:

| Scientist | Key Contribution |
|-----------|------------------|
| **Thales of Miletus** (c. 600 BCE) | Noted static electricity from rubbing amber. |
| **William Gilbert** (1600) | Distinguished between magnetism and electrostatics; coined the term *electricus*. |
| **Benjamin Franklin** (mid‑1700s) | Demonstrated the electrical nature of lightning (kite experiment) and introduced the concept of positive/negative charge. |
| **Alessandro Volta** (1800) | Invented the voltaic pile, the first chemical battery, providing a steady source of electric current. |
| **Hans Christian Ørsted** (1820) | Showed that electric currents produce magnetic fields, linking electricity and magnetism. |
| **Michael Faraday** (1831–1845) | Discovered electromagnetic induction, laying the groundwork for electric generators and motors. |
| **James Clerk Maxwell** (1860s) | Unified electricity, magnetism, and light into a single set of equations. |

So while no single individual “discovered” electricity, the cumulative work of these and many other scientists built the foundation of modern electrical science.
